newsitem.title: ITALY: Versace murder recalls death of Gucci heir.
newsitem.headline: Versace murder recalls death of Gucci heir.

text.p: The killing of world-famous designer Gianni Versace on Tuesday was the second murder in as many years to stun the glamorous world of Italian fashion.
The execution-style shooting by an unknown assassin as Versace entered his mansion in the tourist resort of Miami Beach recalled the 1995 murder of fashion king Maurizio Gucci.
Both men were shot dead in broad daylight.

When Gucci, the last grandson of Guccio Gucci who founded the international fashion dynasty, was shot dead in broad daylight outside his office in Milan in March 1995, it sent shudders through the fashion world.
Police at the time said the attack was carried out by a well-dressed assassin they believed used a pistol with a silencer.
Five people were arrested in connection with Gucci's murder in January this year, including his first wife Patrizia Martinelli, who is charged with commissioning the killing.
Miami Beach Police Chief Richard Barreto said on Tuesday he believed Versace, 50, had been "targeted".
Police said they were looking for a white man aged about 25 who approached Versace and shot him twice in the back of the head from point-blank range.
The motive for the crime was not clear.

Unlike Gucci, who was not a designer himself and had bought out of the family luxury leather goods and fashion empire two years before his murder, Versace remained the lynchpin of his Milan-based operation until his death.
On Tuesday, tributes poured in for the designer who dressed Princess Diana, singers Sting and Elton John, actress Demi Moore and models Elisabeth Hurley and Naomi Campbell and many more.

A star-studded fashion show, planned for Wednesday night on the famous Spanish Steps in Rome as the climax of the city's "alta moda" (haute couture) shows, was called off after the news of Versace's murder.
